assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its translation into incretin therapies is among the most consequential physiological discoveries of recent decades: a gut hormone mechanism became a treatment class that transforms care of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality and clarity are high, and impact is both mechanistic and clinical.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion and action in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor signaling and the therapeutic concept) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide forms) form a plausible trio. Knudsen is credited for the pharmaceutical development of liraglutide and semaglutide, which is industrial and possibly better treated as translation. Other early contributors (such as Habener) are not in the credited list, and priority disputes over the identification of active GLP-1 are not fully resolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature: mechanism confirmed by decades of independent work and large randomized outcome trials, with broad clinical adoption. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Holst, Drucker, Mojsov and the pharmaceutical developers is contested and I have not independently verified priority claims.
Whether the prize should reward physiology, drug development, or both is a judgment call.
Long-term safety and durability data for the newest agents are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave the field a general method for causal, millisecond-precision control of defined cell types, now foundational across neural-circuit research, including motor and spinal circuit analysis, and with early clinical applications in vision restoration. It is highly original, conceptually clear and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: A six-name credit exceeds the three-laureate limit. The channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and the demonstration and development of neuronal use (Deisseroth, Boyden, plus earlier Miesenböck work) are both decisive. My proposed trio balances the molecular tool and its neuroscientific realization but necessarily omits Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, which is a real fairness concern.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independently replicated and used in thousands of studies for over fifteen years, with a stable interpretation of the tool. Clinical translation is still early, but the method itself is established.
uncertainties: Three-person limit leaves several strong contributors out; the optimal configuration is unresolved.
Priority between early photosensitization approaches and channelrhodopsin-based approaches may be disputed.
Clinical impact is so far limited relative to the research impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality, living drugs, with approved products and a rapidly expanding field. The originality and clinical effect are striking.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (design of CD28-costimulated CARs and preclinical proof), June (clinical translation and the CD19 CAR trials) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and TIL therapy, early gene-engineered lymphocyte trials) cover distinct contributions. Early CAR concepts (Eshhar, Gross) are not in the credit list, which complicates fair attribution.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for hematologic cancers with approved products and multi-year follow-up. Solid tumours, toxicity and durability remain open, but the core discovery is established.
uncertainties: Early foundational CAR inventors are outside the supplied credit.
Long-term safety, relapse and secondary malignancy issues persist.
Limited success in solid tumours may temper the scope of the achievement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL in chronic myeloid leukemia converted a fatal disease into a chronically managed one and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, including understanding of resistance and its second-generation solutions.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery and development at Ciba-Geigy), Druker (preclinical specificity and clinical trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) are a natural trio. Credit for the underlying chemistry (e.g. Zimmermann) and for BCR-ABL itself (previously recognized in the Lasker context) lies partly outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with more than two decades of survival data and independent confirmation. Timeliness is excellent, though some may feel the recognition is partly overdue.
uncertainties: The medicinal chemists are not in the credited names.
Whether the committee views this as drug development rather than basic discovery is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed and triggers innate immunity and interferon responses, linking infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and cellular senescence. It is conceptually clean and has opened a large therapeutic field.
assessment.attribution: Chen (identification of cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP), Barber and Ishikawa (identification of STING/MITA) are the decisive contributions; the supplied credit also names Sun and Wu, who were close collaborators on cGAS and cGAMP. I favor the three above, though the cGAS portion is arguably Chen-centred and the STING discovery overlapped with other groups.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: the mechanism is firmly established, but clinical translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet delivered approved drugs, so impact is mostly conceptual so far.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is still pending.
Priority for STING discovery involved several groups, and I have not verified details independently.
Which compound parts of the discovery merit separate recognition is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and are producing large declines in cervical precancer and cancer, a rare example of a preventive vaccine against a human cancer. The principle (self-assembling L1 particles as immunogens) was original and has major public health impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP formation and immunogenicity at the NCI) and Frazer (with Zhou, development of the VLP approach and vaccine) are a plausible trio. Jian Zhou, who died in 1999 and is not listed, was a central contributor to Frazer's work, which complicates attribution. The HPV-cancer link itself was recognized by the 2008 prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature: population-level effectiveness data show strong reductions in cervical disease, and the interpretation is stable. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Zhou's role cannot be recognized by the prize and complicates credit.
Relation to the 2008 recognition of HPV discovery may reduce novelty in the committee's eyes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cancer can arise from blocked cell death rather than only proliferation, defining the apoptosis-regulatory family and leading to BH3-mimetic therapy such as venetoclax. This is a foundational and clinically validated concept.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams (BCL-2 family cloning, characterization and function) and Vaux (BCL-2 as a survival rather than proliferation factor, with early collaboration with Cory) are central. Strasser also contributed substantially. The credited set exceeds three, and Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer, who are not listed, had a key role in identifying BCL-2 in lymphoma. Apoptosis was recognized in 2002 prize, which may limit novelty.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with strong independent confirmation and an approved therapeutic class; timeliness is good, though somewhat late.
uncertainties: Omission of Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer from the supplied credit leaves attribution incomplete.
Partial overlap with the 2002 apoptosis recognition.
Selecting among four credited names is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is a synaptic mechanism for activity-dependent plasticity and an important cellular model of memory; its discovery and later mechanistic dissection (NMDA-receptor dependence) shaped modern synaptic physiology.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo (original 1973 hippocampal demonstration) and Collingridge (NMDA-receptor dependence of LTP) are the most distinct contributions; Morris provided behavioural evidence for the link to learning but that is a separate step. A fair three-person configuration is feasible but debatable.
assessment.maturity: Mature in terms of phenomenon and mechanism, but the extent to which LTP is the mechanism of memory storage in vivo remains debated; the discovery is old, so timeliness is a question rather than a prematurity concern.
uncertainties: Causal link between LTP and memory is still contested.
Distribution of credit between the discovery and the mechanistic work is open.
Whether a decades-old discovery remains competitive with more recent clinical advances is a judgment call.
